text: A challenge is made aloud, by name, before one who counts. A challenge not spoken is not a challenge.
The challenger names the ante. The challenged answers with an ante of equal weight. Weight is judged by the one who must give it.
A challenge formally made may not be refused. It may be deferred up to three days, once.
The challenger names the place. No one may be called to a place they may not enter, unless the challenger invites them in.
One who is bound to a party may stand in that party's place.
The result binds both. The ante is paid at once and in full.
What was taken without a game is owed. Any who counted it may call the debt, and the debtor may not name the terms.
Who plays outside the rules forfeits all antes held.
Where no one counts, nothing was played.
